content: For individuals diagnosed with confirmed high blood pressure, defined as a systolic blood pressure of 130 mmHg or higher and/or a diastolic blood pressure of 80 mmHg or higher, implementing lifestyle modifications is of paramount importance. These modifications include achieving and maintaining weight loss, adhering to the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) diet—which emphasizes a high intake of fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy products—reducing dietary sodium consumption, and increasing potassium intake through dietary sources. In terms of physical activity, it is recommended that individuals engage in at least 150 minutes per week of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise. Additionally, efforts should be made to minimize sedentary behavior by incorporating activities that reduce prolonged periods of inactivity.
